linkedin.title: Most people feel overwhelmed by the news, and it is easy to see why.
linkedin.body:
We are drowning in headlines. Between the constant alerts on our phones and the endless scroll of social feeds, it has become nearly impossible to find the stories that actually impact our lives. The problem is not that there is too much news. The problem is that there is too much noise.

Being informed does not mean reading everything. It means reading what matters to you. When we rely on generic news feeds, we are served a diet of whatever is trending, regardless of whether it is relevant to our careers, our communities, or our personal interests. This creates a false sense of being informed while leaving us missing the details that actually shape our day.

Personalisation is not about building an echo chamber. It is about filtering out the clutter so you can focus on the signal. When technology works correctly, it acts as a curator rather than a gatekeeper. It helps you cut through the static to find the insights you need to make better decisions.

True intelligence is knowing where to direct your attention. We are building Headlinne to make that process simpler, cleaner, and more intentional.

beats.detail: New research reveals a skull secret.
beats.narration: How does your brain actually protect itself from infection? Scientists just found a hidden line of defense.

beats.caption: Researchers found immune hubs tucked inside skull bone marrow.
beats.detail: These cells actively defend the brain.
beats.narration: Researchers discovered special immune hubs tucked deep inside the bone marrow of the skull.

beats.caption: The study was first observed in mouse models.
beats.detail: Testing revealed how they respond to threats.
beats.narration: This was first observed in mice, where these hubs act like a rapid response team.

beats.caption: Similar cells also exist in human skulls.
beats.narration: Crucially, similar cells exist in human skulls too, which suggests we might have the same system.

beats.caption: Their exact role in humans remains unclear.
beats.detail: More research is needed to be sure.
beats.narration: But scientists aren't sure yet if they do the exact same thing in us.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: A visitor to Peru's Allpahuayo-Mishana National Reserve was offered a live owl for sale.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: The offer occurred in 2005, despite commercial hunting being banned in that protected area.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: The incident highlights the ongoing struggle to protect wildlife within established reserves.
